title: Answer a security questionnaire
summary: The 300-row spreadsheet standing between you and the enterprise deal: triage it, pull prior answers and policies from the knowledge base, draft with AI, put the risky answers past security review, and submit in whatever portal the customer demands.

parts.title: Triage the questionnaire, deadline, and deal size
parts.guidance: Identify the customer, service, deadline, required format and commercial significance. Separate factual questions from contractual commitments, sensitive evidence requests and subjects outside the service scope. Assign the questions to security, privacy, legal or engineering as needed and agree any deadline negotiation with the account owner. Drafting can start with the answerable sections while specialist questions remain assigned.

parts.title: Pull prior answers and policies from the knowledge base
parts.guidance: Find prior approved answers, policies, architecture records and audit reports for this service. Check dates and scope before reusing them, and distinguish implemented controls from planned work. Link likely answers to current evidence or an accountable expert. Flag missing evidence and keep confidential reports within their permitted access.

parts.title: Draft answers from the policy corpus
parts.guidance: Answer the customer’s actual questions using current evidence. Add scope or exceptions when a yes-or-no answer would mislead, and leave unsupported claims for the relevant expert. Link consequential answers to their evidence so reviewers can verify them. Keep customer-specific wording distinct from the reusable answer bank, especially when it promises a capability or future action.

parts.title: Security review of the risky answers
parts.guidance: Check assertions about encryption, access, backups, incident response, testing and assurance reports against actual systems and records. Route notification, deletion, location and liability commitments to legal or privacy review. Resolve conflicting answers and record qualified wording or exceptions. The accountable reviewer approves the final answers and evidence attachments before they are represented to the customer.

parts.title: Submit in the customer’s portal
parts.guidance: Submit the approved responses in the verified customer portal through the agreed customer-response process. Check for truncated text, altered formatting and new mandatory attestations. Return new representations to their reviewers before submission. Save the actual submitted copy and receipt, then route follow-up questions to the responsible experts.

parts.title: File the final answers back into the knowledge base
parts.guidance: Add the submitted answers to the knowledge base with the customer, service scope and supporting evidence. Label negotiated concessions with the customer and agreement to which they apply. Mark which product or policy changes would make an answer stale, and preserve the approved submission as the record of what this customer received.

metadata.supportReason: Answer drafting from your policy corpus is highly automatable; the risky answers need a security reviewer and the customer’s portal is manual form work.
